assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new door: a tunable flat-band platform where correlated insulators and superconductivity can be dialled in with a gate and a twist angle. The original experiments, transport and imaging of devices, are independently reproduced in many labs, and the field is a clear discovery rather than a refinement.
assessment.attribution: The theory of the magic angle (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) predicted the flat band; the 2018 transport discovery of correlated states and superconductivity came from the Jarillo-Herrero group. The experimental first author is not among the supplied names, which I flag. The three supplied names form a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: About eight years since the experiments, with wide independent confirmation across platforms and techniques. The interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is still debated, but the existence and control of the phenomena is solid. Timely and not premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit for the 2018 experimental breakthrough extends to junior experimentalists who are not in the supplied list, so the three-person limit forces a difficult choice.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, followed by its experimental observation, created a whole class of materials. It is a prediction confirmed by decisive experiments, which suits a prize built on experimental verification, and it has changed how we classify matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theoretical proposal for graphene and the Z2 classification. Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 3D topological insulator work, are not in the supplied names, so the configuration leaves out some theory credit.
assessment.maturity: Observations in HgTe, followed by ARPES confirmation in Bi-based 3D materials, are well replicated over fifteen or more years. The interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Allocation between the 2D theory, the HgTe experiment and the 3D materials work is contested.
Possible overlap with the already-awarded topological phase theory (2016) may count against it.
Details of the BHZ contribution are from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reached 10^-18 fractional uncertainty. This is a tool that opens doors to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear invention with measurable, verified performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clocks. Ye's group pushed the precision to the 10^-18 level and the quantum many-body clock regime. Both are on the supplied list and form a clean two-person configuration. Other groups (e.g. at NIST, PTB, SYRTE) also contributed, so the scope would need careful wording.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks agree at 10^-18 in several laboratories. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, but the technology is mature and its impact is well documented. Timely.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2005 prize (frequency combs) and the possibility that single-ion clocks are viewed as co-equal should be considered.
Whether the committee wants to honour the lattice concept or the precision record is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in electron optics broke through a limit that had held for sixty years and made sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy routine in TEM and STEM. As a microscopist I know the impact: atoms and their chemical identity are now seen directly across materials, catalysis and devices. This is an invention of the kind the prize was made for.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theory of correctors, Haider the first working TEM corrector, and Krivanek the STEM corrector and its use for atomic-resolution spectroscopy. Together with Urban and Rose and Haider, the credit is spread. The supplied three names give a defensible configuration, though Knut Urban is not in the list. I declare my field, so I weigh this carefully.
assessment.maturity: Correctors are commercially standard and verified in thousands of publications. The sub-angstrom performance is beyond doubt. Maturity is high and recognition is arguably overdue, but the Nobel Prize in Physics 1986 for the electron microscope sets a precedent that a field-defining instrument advance is eligible.
uncertainties: I may be biased as a microscopist and should recuse or be cautious about weighting.
The Chemistry Prize is a possible alternative home.
Allocation of credit between theory and instrument builders is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-quality hexagonal boron nitride crystals became the standard substrate and encapsulant for van der Waals devices. They enabled clean graphene physics, fractional quantum Hall effects, moire physics, and 2D semiconductors. This is an enabling materials discovery with huge impact, though not itself a physical phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: The two names are the sole suppliers of the crystals and co-authors on a large share of the key experiments. The supplied pair is a clean configuration. The risk is whether the committee considers crystal supply a discovery or an invention within the prize's remit.
assessment.maturity: The impact has been verified repeatedly through the work of many groups. It is mature, but a prize for a materials supply would be unusual and would need a clear statement of what the discovery is.
uncertainties: It is uncertain whether this meets the discovery-or-invention bar versus being a service to other discoveries.
The role of other crystal-growth groups is not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect was predicted in magnetic topological insulators and then observed in Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films, giving quantized Hall resistance at zero field. It is an experimentally verified quantum effect with a possible metrological use.
assessment.attribution: Fang and Dai made the key prediction with colleagues (the 2010 paper in Science, with others). Xue's group made the first experimental observation in 2013. The prediction/experiment pairing is clear. Others (Haldane for the original idea, Chang, Zhang) are not in the supplied names or are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in several laboratories, with temperatures still low, and improving through MnBi2Te4. Maturity is good, though the effect is not yet practical.
uncertainties: The credit for the experiment includes Cui-Zu Chang and others who are not in the supplied list.
The prior theoretical origin (Haldane 1988, already honoured in 2016) complicates novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetometer data from Galileo showed induced magnetic fields at Europa, Ganymede and Callisto that require subsurface conducting oceans. It is a measurement-based discovery that has reshaped planetary science and the search for habitable environments.
assessment.attribution: Kivelson led the magnetometer team and Khurana did the key induction analysis. Both are on the list and form a clean pair. Their original discovery paper is clear. The inclusion of a woman scientist is a welcome point, but the decision must rest on the original work.
assessment.maturity: Independent support from later data and modelling, and Europa Clipper and JUICE will test it. The field is not typically a Physics Prize subject. Timing could be premature before the new missions report.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the committee regards this as physics.
Alternative interpretations of the induction signal, such as salty oceans versus other conductors, remain under discussion for Callisto.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, and the 2018 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane map, opened neutrino astronomy. It is an original experiment, large in scale, with verified results.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube, and Spiering was a leader of the earlier detector projects and collaboration. The supplied pair is plausible, but the discovery is a collaborative work of hundreds of scientists, and prior efforts (AMANDA, Baikal, DUMAND) complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed with increasing statistics and by the Galactic plane result. The source identification is only partial. It is mature as a discovery of the flux, but the astronomy is still developing.
uncertainties: Source identification is incomplete.
The large collaboration and its precursors complicate fair credit.
Cosmic-ray and neutrino-detector prizes in 2002 and 2015 set precedents that should be examined.
